title: Recorded edge-streams for SDK contract validation
creator: Priya Patel
body:
Summary:
Produce a set of deterministic, recorded streaming fixtures (token/chunk-level) and a contract validation harness that exercises Python, TypeScript, and Go SDK behaviors for partial responses, backpressure, retries, and graceful cancellation. These fixtures will be used for CI VCR tests and as a contract test baseline against Redwood hosted API to detect regressions in streaming semantics and retry interactions.

Motivation:
- We have recurring, flaky streaming tests across SDKs caused by non-deterministic network timings and intermittent partial chunks during server-side retries.
- Existing replay harnesses assert whole-response equality but miss important client UX flows: mid-stream retries, function-calling metadata emitted mid-stream, incomplete JSON chunks, and client cancellations during buffer flush.
- A language-agnostic, token-granular fixture set allows us to assert client-level invariants (stream ordering, retry dedup, KV-cache resume hints) without invoking live endpoints in CI.

Goals:
- Design a compact fixture format that captures: chunk payload, chunk-level delay, connection resets, HTTP/2 pseudo-headers for trailers, and injected server-retries (302/500 then streamed resume).
- Implement a recorder able to capture real Redwood API streaming sessions (with consent flags) and sanitize PII/keys.
- Provide a validator harness that runs fixture-driven contract checks across Python/TS/Go SDKs and fails CI on behavioral diffs.
- Integrate into monorepo CI (sdk-ci) to run a subset of fixtures on every PR and full suite nightly.

Acceptance criteria (must be all met for Done):
- Fixtures: 20 canonical fixtures covering: full-success fast-stream, slow-token-rate, mid-stream server-retry+resume, partial-JSON-chunk, truncated-connection-with-resume, client-cancel-after-first-3-tokens, function-call-emitted-late, Long-stream-with-kv-cache-hints. Fixture files are human-readable (newline-delimited JSON) and stored at s3://redwood-fixtures/sdk/2026-03/edge-streams/.
- Recorder: CLI recorder (record-stream --out <file>) that can capture a streaming session against a private recording endpoint with TTL-based key, and a sanitizer step that redacts API keys and customer content.
- Harness: test runner (python, node, go) that consumes the fixture format and asserts per-language contracts: token-order, retry-dedup, final-status, metadata-trailers, and retry-backoff-handling.
- CI: PR gate runs 5 fast fixtures matrix'ed across py/ts/go. Nightly pipeline runs full 20-fixture suite. Failure results produce an annotated failure artifact with diffs and trace logs.
- Docs: Confluence doc describing fixture format, recorder usage, and How To add a new fixture (including checklist).

Implementation plan / tasks:
- Task 1: Design fixture schema and reference spec (Priya) (2d)
- Task 2: Implement recorder proxy service and sanitizer (Go small standalone) (Miguel) (4d)
- Task 3: Fixture set creation: record and curate 20 fixtures (hands-on, multi-eng) (Alex Chen + Jordan Lee) (4d)
- Task 4: SDK harness adapters: Python runner + assertions (Jordan) (3d)
- Task 5: SDK harness adapters: TypeScript runner + CI integration (Alex) (3d)
- Task 6: SDK harness adapters: Go runner + integration tests (Miguel) (3d)
- Task 7: CI job authoring and flaky-test handling (rerun thresholds) (SRE) (2d)
- Task 8: Docs + onboarding page + PR template (Priya) (1d)

Test commands (examples):
- Run single fixture locally against Python harness: make -C sdk/python test-fixture FIXTURE=fixtures/slow-token-rate.json
- Nightly job matrix: .github/workflows/sdk-fixtures-nightly.yml runs: make test-fixtures FULL_SUITE=true
- Record a live session (local dev): recorder/record-stream --target https://api.redwood.ai/streams --out my-fixture.json --sanitize

Design notes / trade-offs:
- Format: newline-delimited JSON (NDJSON) is preferred for ease of streaming and git diffs. Each record includes {type:chunk|meta|reset, body:string, delay_ms:int, status:int?(optional)}. Keeping schema minimal avoids coupling to SDK internals.
- Storage: S3 + git pointers for small fixtures. Large captured sessions (>5MB) will be trimmed and kept in long-term S3 only.
- Determinism: We will normalize timestamps and random seeds during recording; the harness will drive the client using the recorded delays to reproduce timing-sensitive behavior.
- Privacy: Sanitizer must remove all user-provided content and replace content with deterministic placeholders. We will keep a strict allowlist for headers.

Risks and mitigations:
- Risk: Recorder may capture sensitive customer data. Mitigation: sanitize step mandatory; recordings encrypted at rest; only infra engineers allowed to generate production recordings.
- Risk: Too many fixtures increases CI time. Mitigation: selective PR gating with small set; full-run nightly and on release branches.
- Risk: SDK implementation differences (Go runtime scheduling vs Node) produce false positives. Mitigation: allow per-language tolerance flags and annotate flaky fixtures.

Deliverables:
- recorder/ (standalone binary + Dockerfile)
- fixtures/2026-03/* (20 canonical NDJSON files)
- sdk-harness/python/fixture_runner.py + assertions
- sdk-harness/js/fixture-runner.ts + assertions
- sdk-harness/go/runner.go + assertions
- CI pipeline entries and failure-reporting artifacts
- Confluence doc + how-to guide

Notes on scope:
This ticket covers the end-to-end prototype and the 20 canonical fixtures plus CI integration. Follow-ups will expand the fixture corpus and add an automated fixture minimizer tool to reduce noisy diffs.
acceptance_criteria: Recorder CLI with sanitizer able to produce sanitized NDJSON
Python/TS/Go harness runners that assert token-order, retry-dedup, metadata trailers
PR CI runs 5 fast fixtures across three languages; nightly runs full 20-fixture suite
Confluence docs explaining format, recorder usage, and how to add fixtures

comments: 2026-02-20 Miguel Santos: Kicked off spike to explore NDJSON schema and existing VCR assets. Found previous recorder code under infra/recorders/ but it only logs whole responses.

2026-02-22 Alex Chen: Prototype of NDJSON schema uploaded to Google Drive: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1-ndjson-proto. Early feedback: include 'stream_id' and 'chunk_index' fields for easier assertions.
2026-02-25 Jordan Lee: Implemented initial Python harness that replays delays and asserts token order. Observed different ordering in Go due to goroutine scheduling; will add tolerance flags.
2026-03-03 Priya Patel: Privacy review requested. Security recommends sanitizer remove email patterns and PII; recording of production sessions requires approval by Security and Customer Ops.
2026-03-08 Miguel Santos: Recorder binary v0.1 implemented and dockerized: ghpr://redwood/infra/recorders/pulls/42. Added basic sanitizer and s3 uploader.
2026-03-10 Priya Patel: Updated acceptance criteria to require CI gating for PRs and nightly full suite. Assigned CI job to SRE for flaky handling.
notes: If the harness finds language-specific non-determinism, mark the fixture as 'lang-tolerant' and add a follow-up to reduce false positives. For now, prefer stricter assertions for core semantics: 'no token duplication after retry' and 'function-call event ordering'.
